immutable.description: Also set the macOS 'uchg' flag on installed files, so even the owner cannot edit, chmod or delete them without 'chflags nouchg'. Write bits are always stripped.

protect.description: How files and templates are locked down after zakwas writes them.

src.description: Source path in the config repo, relative to the directory holding zakwas.yaml (or absolute). May be a directory under 'files'.

dst.description: Destination path: absolute or starting with '~/' (expanded to your home directory). '$VAR' is not expanded. Must not overlap another files/links/templates destination (compared case-insensitively). An existing file zakwas did not write is backed up to '<dst>.zakwas-bak'.

files.description: Repo files installed into your home directory as protected, read-only copies. A directory src copies every file inside it. Edit the source in the repo and run 'zakwas apply' to change one.

src.description: Source path in the config repo, relative to the directory holding zakwas.yaml (or absolute). May be a directory under 'files'.

dst.description: Destination path: absolute or starting with '~/' (expanded to your home directory). '$VAR' is not expanded. Must not overlap another files/links/templates destination (compared case-insensitively). An existing file zakwas did not write is backed up to '<dst>.zakwas-bak'.

links.description: Repo files symlinked into your home directory, for configs an app must be able to write itself. Links are not protected.

vars.description: Values available to every template as '{{ .Vars.<name> }}'. A template referencing a missing var fails.

src.description: Template path in the config repo (Go text/template syntax), relative to the directory holding zakwas.yaml (or absolute).

dst.description: Destination path: absolute or starting with '~/' (expanded to your home directory). '$VAR' is not expanded. Must not overlap another files/links/templates destination.

mode.description: Octal permissions of the rendered file, written with the 0o prefix, e.g. 0o755. Editors parse YAML 1.2 and read 0755 as decimal 755 (zakwas still accepts it as octal); 755 is decimal everywhere. Must be readable by the owner. Write bits are always stripped. Default 0o444.

files.description: Templates to render. Each template also sees '{{ .Home }}', your home directory, and can call the agentPermissions function to render agents.permissions as opencode's permission.bash object and the agentMCP function to render agents.mcp as its mcp object.

templates.description: Go text/template files rendered into your home directory as protected copies, for dotfiles that need your home path or per-machine values.

file.description: Brewfile path in the config repo, relative to the directory holding zakwas.yaml (or absolute). Every third-party tap in it needs 'trusted: true'.

cleanup.description: What to do with installed packages missing from the Brewfile: 'none' keeps them, 'uninstall' removes them ('brew bundle cleanup --force'), 'zap' also removes cask app data ('--zap'). Removals are shown in 'zakwas plan' first. Default none.

upgrade.description: Upgrade outdated Brewfile packages on apply. When false, only missing packages are installed ('--no-upgrade'). Run 'zakwas upgrade' to refresh Homebrew's package list first. Default false.

brew.description: Homebrew packages from a Brewfile. Homebrew is installed first when missing. Omit the section to leave Homebrew alone.

config.description: Global mise config (config.toml) in the config repo, relative to the directory holding zakwas.yaml (or absolute). Its tools are installed with 'mise install'. Install it to ~/.config/mise/config.toml with a 'files' entry so mise uses it outside zakwas too.

prune.description: Remove installed tool versions that no mise config on the machine references anymore ('mise prune'). Default false.

mise.description: Tools pinned in a global mise config. mise is installed first when missing. Omit the section to leave mise alone.

key.description: Preference key within the domain, e.g. 'autohide'.

value.description: Value to write. The YAML type picks the defaults type: true/false → -bool, 2 → -int, 1.5 → -float, anything else → -string. Quote dates ("2024-01-01") and numbers meant as text ("2"); an unquoted date is rejected.

restart.description: Process to 'killall' after the value changes, so it picks up the new setting. Empty uses the built-in mapping (com.apple.dock → Dock, com.apple.finder → Finder, com.apple.screencapture → SystemUIServer).

currentHost.description: Write to the per-host (ByHost) preferences, like 'defaults -currentHost write'. Default false.

defaults.description: macOS preferences written with 'defaults write'. Each domain + key (+ currentHost) may appear once.

path.description: Directory path: absolute or starting with '~/' (expanded to your home directory). '$VAR' is not expanded. Missing parents are created.

mode.description: Octal permissions, written with the 0o prefix, e.g. 0o700. Editors parse YAML 1.2 and read 0700 as decimal 700 (zakwas still accepts it as octal); 700 is decimal everywhere. The owner must be able to read and enter it. When set, it is enforced on an existing directory too. When omitted, a new directory gets 0o755 and an existing one keeps its mode.

sudoTouchID.description: Allow Touch ID for sudo by adding pam_tid.so to /etc/pam.d/sudo_local, which survives macOS updates. Default false.

path.description: Private key path: absolute or starting with '~/' (expanded to your home directory), e.g. '~/.ssh/id_ed25519'.

sshKey.description: Generate an ed25519 SSH key (no passphrase) when the file does not exist. An existing key is never touched.

system.description: Machine-level setup: directories, Touch ID for sudo, an SSH key.

name.description: Label shown in plan and apply output.

check.description: Shell snippet (run with sh in your home directory) that exits 0 when the step is already done. Times out after 30s.

run.description: Shell snippet (run with sh in your home directory) executed while 'check' fails. 'check' must pass afterwards, or apply fails.

commands.description: One-off setup steps: 'run' executes only while 'check' fails. Entries run in order and stop at the first failure.

label.description: Reverse-DNS style job name, e.g. 'com.example.drift-check'. Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'. The plist is written to ~/Library/LaunchAgents/<label>.plist. zakwas only unloads or deletes jobs it created, so a label already loaded from another plist is an error.

program.description: Program and arguments (launchd ProgramArguments). The first entry must be an absolute path or start with '~/'. launchd starts jobs from '/' with a minimal PATH and does not expand '$VAR' or '~', so call a script or '/bin/sh -c' and set 'env' as needed.

every.description: Run at this interval, a Go duration of at least 1m such as '30m' or '6h'. A Mac that was asleep runs the job once on wake, not once per missed interval.

at.description: Run at this local time of day, 'HH:MM' on a 24-hour clock. A Mac that was asleep runs the job on wake.

weekdays.description: Limit 'at' to these days: mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat, sun. Default: every day.

schedule.description: When the job runs: set exactly one of 'every' and 'at'.

runAtLoad.description: Also run the job once whenever it is loaded: at login and after every change to the job. Default false.

env.description: Environment variables for the job, e.g. PATH. Values are written as is, with no expansion.

log.description: File receiving the job's stdout and stderr: absolute or starting with '~/'. launchd creates the file but not its directory. Default: output is discarded.

launchd.description: launchd user agents for scheduled jobs, such as a daily drift check. Each job's plist is written to ~/Library/LaunchAgents and loaded; changing a job reloads it, and removing it unloads it and deletes its plist. Only jobs zakwas created are ever unloaded or deleted. Labels must be unique.

settings.description: Selected global config.toml values using native Codex names. Supports strings, booleans, finite numbers, arrays and nested mappings. Only declared values are updated; omitted values remain. No templates or secret expansion. Profiles, MCP servers, plugins and marketplaces use their dedicated agents fields.

codex.description: Global Codex configuration, applied independently of profiles. Requires explicitly opting in to codex.

providers.description: Providers zakwas manages: claude, codex, opencode, gemini, copilot. Marketplaces target these unless they set their own 'providers'; prune only touches these. codex, gemini and copilot are converged only when named here or in an entry's 'providers'; gemini has no plugin marketplaces, so only its instructions, MCP servers, skills, hooks, permissions and profiles are converged. A provider whose CLI is missing fails its plan; the others still converge. Default: claude, codex and opencode, with codex, gemini and copilot opt-in.

upgrade.description: Update installed plugins to the version their marketplace offers on apply. Run 'zakwas upgrade' to refresh the marketplaces first. Copilot CLI reports no plugin versions, so 'zakwas upgrade' updates its plugins itself, after refreshing the marketplaces. Default false.

prune.description: Remove user-scope plugins and marketplaces that are not declared here, for the managed providers. Plugins installed for a single project, marketplaces they still use, and marketplaces not declared in the provider's user settings are never touched. Removals are shown in 'zakwas plan' first. Default false.

source.description: GitHub 'owner/repo', a git URL, or a local path starting with './', '../', '~/' or '/' (relative paths resolve from the directory holding zakwas.yaml).

providers.description: Providers to add this marketplace to; must be in agents.providers. Default: agents.providers.

marketplaces.description: Marketplaces by name: the name must match the one in the marketplace's own manifest. The value is the source (GitHub 'owner/repo', a git URL, or a local path starting with './', '../', '~/' or '/'; relative paths resolve from the directory holding zakwas.yaml), or an object with 'source' and 'providers'.

id.description: Plugin id 'name@marketplace'; the marketplace must be declared under agents.marketplaces.

providers.description: Providers to install this plugin for; must be targeted by its marketplace. Default: the marketplace's providers.

plugins.description: Plugins to install and enable, each 'name@marketplace' with the marketplace declared under 'marketplaces', or an object with 'id' and 'providers'. A plugin targets its marketplace's providers unless it sets its own.

instructions.description: Global instructions: one file in the config repo, or a list joined in order, each relative to the directory holding zakwas.yaml (or absolute). Every file is a template that sees '{{ .Provider }}' (claude, codex, opencode, gemini, copilot or shared), '{{ .Home }}' and the templates.vars as '{{ .Vars }}'. Each managed provider gets its own rendered, protected copy: claude ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/CLAUDE.md, codex ${CODEX_HOME:-~/.codex}/AGENTS.md (only when codex is named, like its plugins), opencode ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md (best effort unless opencode is named), gemini the context file of its zakwas extension, ${GEMINI_CLI_HOME:-~}/.gemini/zakwas/GEMINI.md (only when gemini is named; ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md is never written), copilot ${COPILOT_HOME:-~/.copilot}/instructions/zakwas.instructions.md (only when copilot is named, with 'applyTo: "**"' added). Claude keeps its '@path' imports, the others get them inlined; a missing import fails the plan, as does a copy over the provider's size limit (codex: 32768 bytes). A file already there is backed up, a link zakwas made is replaced; copies of providers no longer managed are removed.

sharedInstructions.description: Also write the rendered instructions, as provider 'shared', to ~/.agents/AGENTS.md, which Warp, Cline and Factory Droid read, and which Claude, Codex and opencode don't. Needs 'instructions'. Default false.

klaudiush.description: Register klaudiush global hooks for its enabled providers. Zakwas checks registration without running klaudiush during plan and runs 'klaudiush init --install-hooks --global' during apply when needed. Default false.

event.description: Shared lifecycle event: beforeTool, afterTool, sessionStart, or stop. Zakwas maps it to each provider's native event.

command.description: Shell command to run. Use an absolute executable path when the agent may have a different PATH; the command receives provider-specific event JSON on stdin.

providers.description: Providers for this hook; must be in agents.providers. Default: agents.providers, with Codex, Gemini and Copilot opt-in as for plugins.

commands.description: Command hooks declared once for the managed agents. Each command receives provider-specific event JSON on stdin; outputs and blocking behavior remain provider-specific.

hooks.description: Global agent hooks. Commands are declared once and registered with each selected provider; klaudiush remains an optional managed integration.

command.description: Command prefix: one or more words separated by spaces, matched on whole words, e.g. 'git status' matches 'git status --short' but not 'git statusx'. No shell operators, quotes, globs or variables.

providers.description: Providers for this entry; must be in agents.providers. Default: agents.providers, with Codex, Gemini and Copilot opt-in as for plugins.

justification.description: One-line reason Codex shows the agent when the rule prompts for or forbids a command, e.g. 'use git push --force-with-lease'. Gemini CLI shows it for deny rules. Other providers ignore it.

allow.description: Commands the agents run without asking: Claude Code permissions.allow, Codex decision allow (runs outside the sandbox without approval), Gemini CLI decision allow, opencode allow.

command.description: Command prefix: one or more words separated by spaces, matched on whole words, e.g. 'git status' matches 'git status --short' but not 'git statusx'. No shell operators, quotes, globs or variables.

providers.description: Providers for this entry; must be in agents.providers. Default: agents.providers, with Codex, Gemini and Copilot opt-in as for plugins.

justification.description: One-line reason Codex shows the agent when the rule prompts for or forbids a command, e.g. 'use git push --force-with-lease'. Gemini CLI shows it for deny rules. Other providers ignore it.

review.description: Commands that need a review before they run: Codex decision prompt, Gemini CLI decision ask_user, opencode ask. Not written for Claude Code, whose auto mode already reviews every command it doesn't allow.

command.description: Command prefix: one or more words separated by spaces, matched on whole words, e.g. 'git status' matches 'git status --short' but not 'git statusx'. No shell operators, quotes, globs or variables.

providers.description: Providers for this entry; must be in agents.providers. Default: agents.providers, with Codex, Gemini and Copilot opt-in as for plugins.

justification.description: One-line reason Codex shows the agent when the rule prompts for or forbids a command, e.g. 'use git push --force-with-lease'. Gemini CLI shows it for deny rules. Other providers ignore it.

deny.description: Commands the agents must never run: Claude Code permissions.deny, Codex decision forbidden, Gemini CLI decision deny, opencode deny.

permissions.description: Shell command permissions declared once for the managed agents: command prefixes the agents may run without asking (allow), must have reviewed (review) or must never run (deny). Written to Claude Code's settings.json, a Codex rules file and a Gemini CLI user policy file, and to opencode through the agentPermissions template function. Copilot CLI has no user-level shell rules (only root-owned managed settings), so the plan reports them as unsupported for copilot.

command.description: Command that starts a stdio server. Set either 'command' or 'url'.

args.description: Arguments of the command. Written to the agents' config as is, so keep secrets out of them.

env.description: Environment variables set when the command starts, with their values. Written to the agents' config as is, so list secrets under 'envVars' instead.

envVars.description: Names of environment variables passed through from the agent's own environment to the command: Claude Code env NAME=${NAME}, Codex env_vars, Gemini CLI env NAME=$NAME, opencode environment NAME={env:NAME}. Gemini CLI expands $NAME itself, so a server whose command, args, url, env, headers or oauth settings hold a literal '$', or whose name has an underscore, is left out of Gemini CLI and the plan says so.

url.description: URL of an HTTP (streamable) server, http:// or https://, without a user name or password. Written as is, so keep keys out of the query. Set either 'command' or 'url'.

headers.description: HTTP headers with their values. Written to the agents' config as is, so use 'headerEnv' or 'bearerTokenEnv' for secrets.

headerEnv.description: HTTP headers whose value is read from an environment variable: header name to variable name.

bearerTokenEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding a bearer token, sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'.

clientId.description: OAuth client ID registered for this server with its authorization server or gateway. A client ID is public, so it is written to the agents' config as is; the client secret is not supported, only public (PKCE) clients are.

callbackPort.description: Fixed port of the local OAuth callback, for a client whose redirect URIs are registered with a port. Claude Code and opencode take it as callbackPort, Codex as oauth.callback_port, Copilot CLI as auth.redirectPort and Gemini CLI inside redirectUri. Each provider uses its own callback path, so register every redirect URI you sign in with. Default: the provider's own.

scope.description: OAuth scopes to request, separated by single spaces. Default: the scopes the server announces.

oauth.description: The server signs in with OAuth. true only adds the login command to plan and apply, because zakwas never opens a browser; the server registers its own client. A mapping with 'clientId' (and optionally 'callbackPort' and 'scope') also registers that pre-registered public client with every provider that can take it, for a gateway that has no dynamic client registration. Not combined with bearerTokenEnv or an Authorization header. Default false.

providers.description: Providers to register this server with; must be in agents.providers. Default: agents.providers, with Codex, Gemini and Copilot opt-in as for plugins.

mcp.description: MCP servers by name, each a stdio server ('command') or an HTTP server ('url'), declared once for the managed agents. Registered at user scope in Claude Code (~/.claude.json), Codex (config.toml, edited in place) and Copilot CLI (${COPILOT_HOME:-~/.copilot}/mcp-config.json, edited in place), in the zakwas extension of Gemini CLI, and in opencode through the agentMCP template function. Secrets are never written: name the environment variables that hold them. A server of the same name that zakwas did not add is adopted when identical and fails the plan when it differs; removing a server here removes only servers zakwas added.

description.description: One line on what the profile is for. Claude Code and opencode show it; Codex profiles carry no description.

prompt.description: File in the config repo (relative to the directory holding zakwas.yaml, or absolute) with the profile's instructions. A template that sees '{{ .Provider }}', '{{ .Home }}' and the templates.vars as '{{ .Vars }}'. Written as the body of the Claude Code and opencode agent files and as Codex developer_instructions. Claude Code replaces its default system prompt with it.

tools.description: Abstract tools the profile may use: read, search (glob and grep), edit, shell, web. Omit for all of them. Claude Code gets a tools list and opencode denies the others; Codex cannot restrict tools.

edit.description: File edits: allow, ask or deny. Claude Code: acceptEdits, default, or the edit tools removed. opencode: its edit permission. Codex: sandbox read-only for deny, workspace-write for allow; ask is not expressible.

shell.description: Shell commands: allow, ask or deny. opencode: bash permission, with agents.permissions applied; Claude Code: ask is its default, deny removes Bash, allow is not expressible. Codex: approval_policy never for allow and on-request for ask; deny is not expressible.

sandbox.description: Codex sandbox mode. Default: read-only when edit is deny, workspace-write when it is allow. Claude Code and opencode have no sandbox.

network.description: Network access. Codex: sandbox_workspace_write.network_access. Claude Code and opencode: false removes the web tools, but their shell commands stay unrestricted.

reviewer.description: Who approves what needs approval: user, or auto, an automatic reviewer. Claude Code: permission mode auto; Codex: approvals_reviewer auto_review; opencode has none.

mcp.description: Access to each MCP server declared under 'mcp': allow, ask or deny. A declared server not listed is denied. Codex: enabled and default_tools_approval_mode; Claude Code: the server's tools in or out of the profile (allow is not expressible, its tools ask); opencode: a '<server>_*' permission.

providers.description: Providers to render the profile for; must be in agents.providers. Default: agents.providers, with Codex, Gemini and Copilot opt-in as for plugins.

model.description: Model for this provider, in its own spelling, e.g. 'sonnet' for Claude Code, 'gpt-5' for Codex, 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4' for opencode.

overrides.description: Extra top-level frontmatter keys (Claude Code, opencode) or settings (Codex), written as is. Values are re-typed by YAML, so quote ones that must stay strings (dates, versions). A key zakwas sets from the profile's own fields is rejected.

claude.description: Claude Code only: model and extra frontmatter.

model.description: Model for this provider, in its own spelling, e.g. 'sonnet' for Claude Code, 'gpt-5' for Codex, 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4' for opencode.

overrides.description: Extra top-level frontmatter keys (Claude Code, opencode) or settings (Codex), written as is. Values are re-typed by YAML, so quote ones that must stay strings (dates, versions). A key zakwas sets from the profile's own fields is rejected.

codex.description: Codex only: model and extra profile settings.

model.description: Model for this provider, in its own spelling, e.g. 'sonnet' for Claude Code, 'gpt-5' for Codex, 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4' for opencode.

overrides.description: Extra top-level frontmatter keys (Claude Code, opencode) or settings (Codex), written as is. Values are re-typed by YAML, so quote ones that must stay strings (dates, versions). A key zakwas sets from the profile's own fields is rejected.

opencode.description: opencode only: model and extra frontmatter.

model.description: Model for this provider, in its own spelling, e.g. 'sonnet' for Claude Code, 'gpt-5' for Codex, 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4' for opencode.

overrides.description: Extra top-level frontmatter keys (Claude Code, opencode) or settings (Codex), written as is. Values are re-typed by YAML, so quote ones that must stay strings (dates, versions). A key zakwas sets from the profile's own fields is rejected.

gemini.description: Gemini CLI only: model and extra frontmatter of its subagent file, such as temperature or max_turns.

model.description: Model for this provider, in its own spelling, e.g. 'sonnet' for Claude Code, 'gpt-5' for Codex, 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4' for opencode.

overrides.description: Extra top-level frontmatter keys (Claude Code, opencode) or settings (Codex), written as is. Values are re-typed by YAML, so quote ones that must stay strings (dates, versions). A key zakwas sets from the profile's own fields is rejected.

copilot.description: Copilot CLI only: model and extra frontmatter of its agent file.

profiles.description: Agent profiles by name, each declared once and rendered for every managed provider: a Claude Code subagent file in ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/agents/zakwas/<name>.md (start it with 'claude --agent <name>'), a Codex profile file ${CODEX_HOME:-~/.codex}/<name>.config.toml ('codex --profile <name>', only when codex is named) an opencode agent file ~/.config/opencode/agents/<name>.md ('opencode --agent <name>', best effort unless opencode is named) a Gemini CLI subagent file ${GEMINI_CLI_HOME:-~}/.gemini/zakwas/agents/<name>.md (delegate with '@<name>', only when gemini is named) and a Copilot CLI agent file ${COPILOT_HOME:-~/.copilot}/agents/<name>.agent.md ('copilot --agent <name>', only when copilot is named). A profile denies every server declared under 'mcp' that it does not list; servers added outside zakwas are not affected. The plan names, per provider, every profile field that provider cannot express. A profile name may be at most 64 characters, and a profile name an opencode template also defines under 'agent' fails the plan, as does a profile file that a 'files', 'links' or 'templates' destination also writes. Removing a profile removes only the files zakwas rendered.

path.description: Skill directory holding SKILL.md, named like the skill. Without 'git': relative to the directory holding zakwas.yaml, or absolute or '~/...'. With 'git': a relative path inside the repository.

git.description: Git source of the skill: GitHub 'owner/repo' or a clone URL. zakwas clones it on apply into ~/.local/share/zakwas/skills and pulls it on 'zakwas upgrade'. Omit for a skill on disk.

ref.description: Branch or tag to clone, only with 'git'. Default: the repository's default branch.

providers.description: Providers to link this skill for; must be in agents.providers. Default: agents.providers, with Codex, Gemini and Copilot opt-in as for plugins. Codex, opencode and Copilot share ~/.agents/skills.

skills.description: Standalone skills, which don't come from a plugin marketplace, linked into every managed agent's skills directory: Claude Code's ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/skills, and ~/.agents/skills for Codex, opencode and Gemini CLI (${GEMINI_CLI_HOME:-~}/.agents/skills when GEMINI_CLI_HOME is set), and for Copilot CLI too unless COPILOT_HOME is set, which then reads ${COPILOT_HOME}/skills only. Each entry is a skill directory (holding SKILL.md) in the config repo or elsewhere on disk, or an object with 'git', 'path' and optional 'ref' for a skill inside a git repository. The directory name must equal the name in SKILL.md, and names are unique. zakwas replaces nothing it did not link; a skill directory or link already there fails the plan. 'plan' never fetches, 'apply' clones missing git sources and 'zakwas upgrade' pulls them.

skillsDir.description: Directory opencode loads user skills from, absolute or '~/...'. Default: ~/.config/opencode/skills. OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR is ignored, since tools like Orca set it to a private config; set this instead to install elsewhere.

guard.description: Stop the managed agents from applying this config themselves. An agent that can run 'zakwas apply' can widen its own permissions, add hooks or install marketplaces, because apply writes agent config files the agent may not edit. While on, every managed agent is denied 'zakwas apply', 'upgrade', 'self-update', 'approve' and 'mcp' (Claude Code in settings.json, Codex in its rules file, Gemini CLI in its user policy file, opencode through the agentPermissions template function), Claude Code is denied edits to the config repo's main checkout and to zakwas state, and 'zakwas apply' and 'upgrade' started from an agent session refuse. 'plan' and 'check' stay allowed. The plan names a managed provider that cannot be protected, such as Copilot CLI, which has no user-level deny rules and is covered only by the refusal. Default true; false removes the rules zakwas added.

agents.description: Coding-agent plugins and the marketplaces they come from, converged per provider: claude (Claude Code), codex (Codex) and opencode (skills linked into its skills directory). Omit the section to leave agent plugins alone.

title: zakwas.yaml
description: Declarative macOS setup converged by zakwas: files, links, templates, brew, mise, agents, defaults, system, commands, launchd.
